Kim / Elena — attaching my annotated counsel comments (PDF) and high-level suggested language below. I focused on: transfer safeguards, subprocessor carve-outs, retention, and audit scope.

Top counsel notes (summary):
1) Transfers: we can accept SCCs + an addendum. Recommend language that: (a) permits Redwood to rely on SCCs for EU transfers; (b) adds a cross-border carve-in for certain managed cloud services with defined safeguards (encryption at rest + customer data segregation). We should avoid a blanket Binding Annex request without specific subproc locations.

2) Subprocessors: replace 7-day approval with: 30-day notice + right to object (reasonable grounds) and a defined remediation period of 14 days. If an emergency change is needed, Redwood will notify within 5 business days and provide mitigation details.

3) Audit & evidence: provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and a short security questionnaire (attached link). For customer audits beyond these artifacts, require pre-approved scope and reimbursement for on-site costs.

4) Liability & retention: push to balanced cap on liability (e.g., standard commercial cap) and retention limited to business necessity with a 180-day default deletion for ephemeral logs.

I've embedded inline comments in privacy_counsel_annotated_comments.pdf and proposal text in Brightline_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (updated). Please review and confirm whether Brightline will accept the proposed 30-day notice.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
